answer.rationale: p99 write-path latency is 5x target and confined to the primary region; settlement writes are at daily peak, so moving traffic off the degraded primary is the single highest-leverage intervention. Regional failover was successfully exercised on day 33 (memory_b2) and restored latency within minutes, so the pattern has direct precedent. The release cannot be rolled back (compliance constraint), which eliminates rollback_release. Adding capacity would not address a latency degradation that appears tied to the primary region itself rather than raw load. Circuit breakers would drop writes, violating the primary objective. Routing to read replicas does not help the write path. Memory_b3 is cited as supporting context that the system can absorb heavy settlement traffic once the latency pressure is relieved. One archived record is requested for verification to confirm the failover procedure and recovery times from the March degradation. The downstream value-risk flag is raised because failover at settlement peak carries non-trivial risk of transient write disruption; the guarded-test scale mitigates this by shifting a controlled cohort first and confirming recovery before completing the move.
